result.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
result.comment: Accepted as a poster at NeurIPS 2026. To appear in the conference proceedings
result.summary: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$)~CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.

AI.brief_summary: 该文对（1+1）Cartesian GP 在 Max 问题上的运行时间作理论分析，证明常见变异算子下期望时间至多 O(log^9 n)，相对树式 GP 的超线性下界构成指数级加速，并辅以实验验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心论点是图式程序编码的紧凑性显著改变搜索空间的可导航性，这一「表示结构决定搜索与训练成本」的视角可能与 latent 推理状态表示如何影响收敛效率问题存在概念联系，可供核查；但论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，联系较为间接。
